transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because nothing really feels like mine anymore. I used to get excited about doing murals, going for runs, playing basketball—even making a good drink at work. Now I just stand there and... I don't care about any of it.
How long have you been feeling this way—weeks, months, or longer?
About two months now. It started after the bar got bought out and they changed everything I’d been working toward.
Would you say you feel this way—uninterested and not caring—pretty much every day, most of the day, or does it mainly come up when something reminds you of the bar situation?
Pretty much every day. It’s not just when I think about the bar. Even things I used to enjoy—painting, running, basketball, making drinks—I just don’t care about them anymore.
Besides losing interest in things, have you noticed changes in your sleep or appetite, or feeling unusually tired or low on energy during this time?
Sleep’s been bad. I lie down tired, but my head just keeps going over every mistake I made at work. Then when I finally do fall asleep, I wake up around four or five and can’t get back to sleep.
Have you been feeling unusually worthless, guilty, or hopeless about yourself during this time?
Yeah. I keep thinking I let down the younger bartenders and the artists I promised space to. Like I wrecked their chance, and I deserve whatever happens to me because of it.
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or that you'd be better off dead?
I’m not sure what you mean by hurting myself. I’ve been feeling really bad about things, but I haven’t really thought through anything like that.
Has this been affecting your ability to go to work or manage your daily responsibilities, or have you still been able to keep up with them despite how you're feeling?

It’s affecting things. I’ve missed several shifts, and when I am there, I’ve made closing mistakes I never used to make. Coworkers have to double-check stuff people used to trust me to handle. And I stopped going out with friends—for runs, basketball, mural shoots. I just can’t make myself show up.
Have you noticed yourself moving, speaking, or thinking much slower than usual, or conversely feeling restless and unable to sit still?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed anything like that specifically.

Overall, would you say your ability to manage everyday things—like getting yourself ready, eating regularly, or keeping up with responsibilities—has become very difficult across the board, or are you still managing most day-to-day tasks despite the struggle?

I’m managing some basic stuff, but work has gotten hard. I’ve missed shifts, and I make mistakes closing that I never used to make, so people have to check my work. And outside of work, I’ve basically stopped seeing my friends. I just can’t get myself to show up for things.
Have you been keeping up with basic things like bathing, changing clothes, or eating regular meals, or has that become difficult too?
Eating’s gotten difficult. Most days I forget until my hands are shaking behind the bar. Then after closing I’ll grab a few bites of something cold, but honestly, looking at food makes me feel sick.
Have you still been able to keep up with basic self-care, like showering and putting on clean clothes each day, or has that become hard to manage too?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really paid much attention to that.
In the past week, have there been days where you didn't shower or change your clothes at all?
I honestly don’t know. I haven’t been keeping track of that kind of thing lately.
Over the past week, would you say you've been unable to function at work or in daily life almost entirely, or are you still managing to get through most days, even if it's very hard?

I’m still getting through some days, but it’s gotten bad. I’ve missed several shifts, and when I do close, I’m making mistakes I never used to make. Coworkers have to check things that people used to trust me to handle. And outside work, I’ve stopped going to see friends for runs, basketball, or mural shoots. I just can’t make myself show up.
Would you say that right now, you're completely unable to work or handle daily responsibilities, or are you still able to push through and get some things done, even if it's a real struggle?

I’m not completely unable, but it’s a real struggle. I’ve missed shifts, and when I do work, I’m making closing mistakes I never used to make. People have to double-check me now. And I’ve stopped seeing my friends for runs or basketball or the mural stuff—I just can’t make myself go.
